rationale: Frozen objective is ttft_ms on a single leased RTX 4090 (Qwen3-4B BF16 SDPA, batch=1, 256-token GPU-resident prompt, prefill + argmax between two explicit torch.cuda.synchronize calls at qwen_inference.py:16-24). The torch collector already ran and coverage.json shows 66,441 CUDA kernels fully associated (0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences, 0 autograd ranges), so kernel-level attribution is already complete and single-stream inference raises no overlap, CUDA-graph-tracing or attribution question that nsys would resolve. The open diagnostic question for TTFT is attribution inside the prefill window: GPU kernel execution versus host submission gaps across the per-layer dispatch of the 36-layer forward plus argmax before the first-token-ready synchronize. execution_timeline answers this with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, submit-gap intervals, synchronization events, per-device intervals and clock-alignment bounds; python_runtime then localizes any host-side dispatch/binding cost (transformers Qwen3 forward path, SDPA dispatch, KV-cache handling) via its warmed cProfile trace, used only for host attribution since its times are perturbed and are not GPU durations. Collectors declined with reasons: nccl_tuning and collective_calibration (no collectives; communication not_applicable for a single-device task), device_telemetry (device-wide NVML samples with native windows cannot attribute the short single-GPU prefill and no in-window host transfer exists; per-collective bytes unobservable and not derived from payload sizes), binding_cost and candidate_diagnostics (no candidate exists yet), and torch (already collected).
